newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says economy continues expansion in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Germany says economy continues expansion in Q3.

text.p: Continued strong foreign orders for German products fuelled further expansion of the economy in the third quarter of 1996, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.
German gross domestic product (GDP) probably rose around two percent in real terms from the same quarter a year earlier after a rise of 1.2 percent year-on-year in the second quarter.
The ministry added that third quarter GDP "clearly rose" against the second quarter, but that the rate of growth was lower than the quarter-on-quarter growth in the previous three months.
Preliminary statements on quarter-on-quarter changes were based on seasonal and price-adjusted data.
"The driving force behind economic expansion was foreign stimulus after the middle of the year," the ministry said in its monthly report.
The report said foreign industry orders rose a strong five percent in the third quarter compared to the previous quarter.
"In addition to a more dynamic world economy, the improvements in the competitiveness of German producers had a positive effect," the ministry said.
It added that German companies benefitted from "normalisation of the mark exchange rates and moderate wage developments" in west Germany.

The ministry also said it was not surprising the rate of growth in the third-quarter growth was less than in the second, which was marked by "normalisation of economic activity after the cold winter."
